methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $100M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Arc Boats is a Series B stage transportation company founded by Mitch Lee and Ryan Cook that has raised $100M+. The valuation exercise draws on a comparable universe of 7 private frontier-tech transportation firms—including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, The ePlane Company, and DeepDive—though no public market comparables exist in this nascent sector.

Stage-progression methodology was the applicable triangulation approach. Using the $100M total capital raised as a base value proxy and applying a typical Series B step-up multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $190M. Peer-median analysis was not executable; while the transportation sector contains 3 peers, none met narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier valuation bandwidth), and relying on all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable methodological noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $162M (low) to $218M (high), with a median point of $190M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result given single-method reliance. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage transportation peers suitable for median benchmarking and the degree to which $100M in cumulative raise accurately reflects current enterprise value. Investors should weight this estimate accordingly against operational metrics, unit economics, and capital efficiency data not present in this valuation framework.
